explanation: The act by which God regards a sinful person as righteous solely on the basis of faith, not through their own works or the demands of the law.
A firm conviction and trust in God's promises and character, especially regarding Jesus' death and resurrection for the sake of sins.
The actions a person performs in an attempt to serve or earn God's favor through the law; these are considered insufficient for salvation.
The father of the Jewish people and the central figure in the chapter, presented as a model for all believers because he was counted righteous before circumcision took place.
The physical sign of the covenant between God and Abraham; Paul uses this to show that righteousness comes through faith independently of religious rituals or ethnicity.
Evil actions, violations of God's law, and a universal human condition that separates people from God and requires reconciliation.
God's undeserved favor and goodwill given to people without them having earned it or being able to repay it through their own efforts.
Moses' law (Torah) with its demands and commandments; the chapter argues that the law does not give life, but reveals sin.
The physical end of life as a consequence of sin, as well as the spiritual separation from God before salvation was achieved through Christ.
The event where Jesus rose from the dead; this is the basis for believers being justified and given eternal life.
